targets.title: Word predictability effects are linear, not logarithmic: Implications for probabilistic models of sentence comprehension.
targets.evidence_quote: The primary aim of our study was to assess whether BK’s finding of a linear relationship between predictability and reading time, obtained using the SPR paradigm, would replicate if the same items are used in the more naturalistic eyetracking paradigm.
targets.outcome_quote: Contrary to BK’s results, we found support for a logarithmic relationship between contextual predictability and the eye movement measures of first fixation duration and gaze duration, as well as less definitive support for a logarithmic relationship with the word skipping measure.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The central linear relationship is explicitly contradicted by the logarithmic relationship in the new eyetracking sample.
